discipline: The theory's own grammar and its director's direction (AI-written). Read for this: AGENTS.md; 08-METHOD section 1; 01-ROOT sections 1 to 3; the situation schema in situations.json; the seven guidance notes; Ren's words of 11 November; places-v1.json; all 88 decisions; the checkers' remarks; dynamics.json (region C in full, families A, E, F by entry, H by name); premises.json; and ten Lean statements (ReadsShare, Locked, Unread, uniform_locks, lock_outlives_loss, window_never_read, pool_closes_gap, scheduled_apart, separates_all_iff_member, never_locked). Counts below were computed read-only from those files. The assignment of items to relations is my reading in one pass, not put to a second reader.
verdict_on_present:
What it gets right, and should be kept whatever else changes:
- Plain names with an everyday example ("Those who would notice are gone") are handles a person keeps.
- Every mark was settled against its Lean statement and put to a second reader to refute.
- Line style says how far seen.
- 12 items were left unresolved instead of forced, and the hole is drawn.
- Ren recognised it as a map.

Where it falls short as a data structure: the 15 places are not one kind of thing, and the list cannot say so.
- Some are one relation with one value: "uncounted" (what is used up reaches no one with a say), "fixed-rule".
- Some are conjunctions: "judged-inside" is "holds-itself" + "uncounted" + who judges. A checker found that no single law of closed-capture carries both halves.
- Some are the two sides of one threshold listed as two places: shaping-costs / shaping-pays, several-ways / all-on-one, and felt / past-turning-back, which differ only in timing.

The checkers' remarks are mostly this one finding repeated: overlap, forks that one decision cannot hold, the same threshold drawn several times, and 12 of the 16 "inside" items piled in holds-itself because its inner structure has no home.

As a picture, a node-link map of places is one of the right projections. As the stored structure it is dominated: a structure keyed on the relations can regenerate this map by script, and this map cannot regenerate the relations.
dominated_where: Faithfulness, duplicates: 7 of the 38 arrows are one threshold (does a costly practice bring its doers back what it costs) drawn as 4 arrows shaping-costs to shaping-pays and 3 back, from RuleShaping.favours_iff, stretch_iff, grouped_rises_iff, grouped_rises_iff_sized, DrawnShaping.favours_everywhere_iff, PairSelection.assorted_favours_iff and window_echo_select_iff. A checker asked for exactly this: cases on one arrow, not parallel arrows.

Faithfulness, forks: one exact law with two outcomes is split or half-lost. Thinned.kept_iff is drawn twice (readers-drawn-from-the-selected exit 1 as felt to cost-counts, transition 2 as felt to past-turning-back). Web.readableInTime_iff (reading-a-loss-in-time transition 1) keeps one head as an arrow and the other, equally exact, in a note.

Faithfulness, skipped steps: 5 arrows into cost-counts (2 from judged-inside, 2 from holds-itself, 1 from noticers-gone) cross two relations at once. ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss takes "the rule's reading does not favour once the loss passes a bound" as a premise (it drops Unread) and shows only that the rule then turns. How the loss comes to reach anyone with a say is other laws in another model (Web). The solid arrow hides that join.

Faithfulness, silent identifications: putting ClosedCapture's Unread and Web's "selected alike through every member's couplings" on the same node "felt" is a reading. The atlas says so itself (reading-a-loss-in-time exit 4), and that item sits among the 12 unresolved instead of being shown as what licenses the node.

Direction and the dualism concern: the picture runs from sources to sinks. No arrow enters holds-itself, judged-inside, uncounted or fixed-rule; cost-counts (8 in), past-turning-back (5 in) and ended (2 in) have none out. That reads as one good ending and two bad ones. It comes from the atlas listing only exits. A checker names a proved course back out of cost-counts (Drained.strong_undone) that is not an item.

Use: a real case is usually in several places at once (a checker: the two sides of the tipping count are holds-itself AND shaping-pays or shaping-costs), and 15 prose tests give no way to say so. The one worked case in situations.json is located by 40 Lean-level premises, 36 of them "not checked", with all 3 exits "not read". No person can use that.

Economy: 15 places with free-text tests, 5 kinds of decision and free-text conditions, where about 10 relations with 2 or 3 values each and 3 kinds of law item carry the same 88 decisions. At region scale that is cleaner types more than fewer things.

Scaling: places are per region. At 183 dynamics a flat list reaches 35 to 40 with more overlap. Relations are shared across families: family E's giving-against-keeping is already on region C's return-against-cost threshold by two proved identities (PairSelection.assorted_counts, window_echo_shaped), which the flat structure had to leave unresolved as "compose".

Layout: positions are hand-set and mean nothing. With relations stored, position can carry meaning (one axis per relation, or neighbours differing in one relation) and containment can be drawn as nesting instead of as two boxes.
Not dominated: route-finding at a glance (where can this go in two steps) and memorable names. Keep the place graph as a generated projection and keep the names.
proposal_in_one_paragraph: Store the relations and derive the places. In the account's own grammar a place is not a thing but a shape of relations in a web: who sets the rule and from what, who judges, who draws on what, what reaches whom, who is among those with a say, and when. That is the situation schema (formations, conditions, couplings, readers with reads / drawn_from / selects, rule, time, bears) with roles in place of actual parties. So use one schema for both: a place is a small situation with roles for names, each relation set to a value or left free. A change is one relation appearing, ending or changing value, given the others, under a law. A real case is an actual web with its parties bound to the roles; it lies in every place whose pattern it matches, so overlap is native. In 01's terms each relation with its values is a class, staying is a line under that class that does not end, and a change is the line ending under one class while it continues under the others. The Lean already states the hold and its exit this way (ClosedCapture.lock_line, loss_ends_line), so no new primitive is added. The 15 names stay as names of patterns; their free-text tests go.
drawn_from_it:
Two things.

1. The figure. One small web for the region: six roles as nodes (those ahead, the others, the rule, those with a say, what is used up, those who depend on it) and the relations as numbered edges. Then the named places as a strip of small copies of that same web, each with its edges on, off or faint (free), ordered so neighbours differ in one edge. The changed edge is drawn in the law's line style. Clicking an edge shows what makes it appear, what ends it and what keeps it, both directions, with "no law" written where there is none. The topology is in each node, and a change is seen as an edge appearing or ending. The present node-link map is generated beside it for routes.

2. The sheet. The relations as about ten questions with their answers. The same table is read three ways:
- asked of a real case, it locates the case on the map;
- per place, it is the skeleton of the short article (which answers, what changes each, what keeps each, which places contain it);
- per relation and direction with law counts, it shows what is missing.

On the Changes, soberly. The representational idea fits and the checkers' remarks are evidence for it: a situation is several aspects at once, and a change is one aspect changing given the others. All 38 arrows sort onto seven relations. Three things do not fit:
- A hexagram sets every line and all 64 exist. Here most combinations have no law and a place leaves most relations free.
- The lines of a hexagram are independent and ordered by position. These relations depend on one another (the loss can reach someone with a say only through a member it reaches: Web.separates_all_iff_member), some have three values, and many laws are thresholds on counts.
- The account already has the 64 hexagrams as a named model (Becoming.Hexagrams, 06 section 5), so drawing places as hexagrams would confuse the two and add vocabulary.

So take "few aspects, one changes given the others" and leave the six-line glyph and the names. A small web shows who relates to whom, which a stack of lines hides.
worked_sample:
Roles: A those ahead under the rule; O the others; R the rule; J those whose judgment enters the rule; X what is used up that the rule does not count; D those who depend on X.

Relations:
r1. R from results: is the rule rebuilt from what it picked? no / yes. Lean: RuleCapture.ReadsShare.
r2. R favours: whom does the rule in force favour? those ahead / not them / swings. Lean: RuleCapture.Locked; Alternating.never_locked.
r3. J from: who has a say? drawn from those ahead / the others too / a fixed list of all who began. Lean: the drawn pool, Thinned.
r4. A draws on X: is something used up that the rule does not count, and growing? yes / no. Lean: ClosedCapture.Accrues.
r5. X reaches J: does it make a difference to anyone with a say? no one / someone. Lean: ClosedCapture.Unread; Web selected-alike.
r6. D among J: are those who depend on it among those with a say? never asked / in / removed.
r7. time: can it still be kept? before / past.
r8. return: does a costly practice bring its doers back what it costs? yes / no.
r9. ways in use: several / one.
r10. goes on: yes / no.

Eight places as patterns:
- fixed-rule = {r1 no}
- holds-itself = {r1 yes, r2 those ahead}
- uncounted = {r4 yes, r5 no one}
- judged-inside = {r1 yes, r2 those ahead, r3 from those ahead, r4 yes, r5 no one}. This is holds-itself and uncounted and r3: a containment, which the flat map draws as three separate boxes.
- noticers-gone = {r6 removed or never asked}
- felt = {r5 someone, r7 before, r2 those ahead}
- cost-counts = {r5 someone, r2 not them}
- past-turning-back = {r7 past, r2 those ahead}
- shaping-pays and shaping-costs = r8 yes and r8 no: one relation.

Nine law items:
1. turn r5 no one to someone, given some member of J is reached; exact. Web.separates_all_iff_member (unselected-beyond-the-coupling-closure exit 1). Flat: uncounted to felt.
2. turn r6 never asked to in, and so r5 someone; witness. Clearing.pool_closes_gap, PoolCourse.scheduled_apart (same dynamic, exits 2 and 3; both drop flow-pool-within-group-closure-either). Flat: the same uncounted to felt arrow as item 1, though a different relation moves. The docstring adds that being told apart does not make the loss good.
3. fork on r7 when r5 turns: before gives felt, past gives past-turning-back; exact. Web.readableInTime_iff (reading-a-loss-in-time transition 1). Flat: one head drawn, one in a note.
4. fork on r2, given r5 someone and r3 the others too: the rule turns exactly when those ahead are the fewer among those with a say when the loss is counted, otherwise it is kept; exact. ClosedCapture.Thinned.kept_iff (readers-drawn-from-the-selected exit 1 and transition 2). Flat: two arrows.
5. turn r2 those ahead to not them, given r4 yes, a reading that does not favour once the loss passes a bound, and a rebuilding after that bound; sufficient. ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss (closed-capture exit 1; a-counter-rule-read-from-its-own-share exit 2; drops closedcapture-unread). Flat: judged-inside to cost-counts and holds-itself to cost-counts. The law takes r5 as given; items 1 to 3 show r5, in another model.
6. join of 5 with 1 to 3: reading-a-loss-in-time exit 4 and compose 1; a reading. Flat: unresolved.
7. turn r2 to those ahead from any start, given r1 yes and a reading that favours them at every share, by the step after the second rebuilding; sufficient. RuleCapture.uniform_locks (capture-through-the-rule transition 1). Flat: "inside holds-itself", because "any start" is not a place.
8. hold r2 those ahead and r5 no one, given r1 yes, r4 yes and r6 removed before they register it (K ≤ N); sufficient. PoolFromCourse.window_never_read (the-lock-draws-its-readers-out transition 1). Flat: "stays" in noticers-gone. With: turn r6 in to removed, given X is what D lives on; witness. ReadingsSpread.Commons.cleared_spreads (readings-revised-spread-and-locked exit 4).
9. turn r8 both ways; exact. RuleShaping.favours_iff / disfavours_iff (shaping-the-rule-selected-by-what-comes-back transition 1), with six further cases: transitions 2, 4, 5; shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected transition 2; offspring-read-from-giving-that-waits transitions 1 and 2, the last two joined by proved identities (compose 1 and 2, flat: unresolved). Seven arrows and two unresolved items become one relation, seven cases and two proved joins.

Tally:
- All 38 arrows are changes of seven relations: r2 11, r8 7, r9 7, r5 6, r6 3, r7 2, r10 2.
- Of the 12 unresolved, 6 become join records: 2 proved, 3 readings, 1 open.

A real case, read from situations.json's own fields (my reading, not checked): the reward-model pipeline is written as one pass, so r1 no. Users and third parties bear what lies beyond every rater's couplings, so r5 no one and r6 never asked. It is in fixed-rule and uncounted at once and not in holds-itself as written; r1 would turn if the reward model were refit to the deployed policy's own outputs. That is four answers, where the file now carries 36 premises "not checked".
what_it_reveals:
1. The hole, exactly. "No law gives an arrow into the hold" splits in two.
- The rule coming to favour those ahead has a law, given the rule is rebuilt from its results (uniform_locks, item 7).
- What has no law either way is r1 itself. ReadsShare is taken by 18 laws in 5 dynamics and dropped by no exit anywhere in the atlas.
- The same is true of r4: Accrues is taken by 22 laws in 7 dynamics, dropped by no exit, and has no model listed where it fails. No recorded way out is "the drawing stops".
- And of r3: the drawn pool is taken by 31 laws in 4 dynamics, dropped by none, with no model listed where it holds.
Three relations that every law of the region stands on and none turns. closed-capture's own "open" list says the first in words; the place map cannot show it, because premises are not places.

2. A loop the boxes hide. It runs through four relations of one situation: those ahead draw on X (r4); that removes those who depend on X from those with a say (r6: one witness, two readings); so X reaches no one with a say (r5, held by window_never_read); so the rule keeps favouring those ahead (r2, lock_outlives_loss). Three links carry laws. The fourth, that the favoured side keeps drawing, is the premise Accrues in every one of them.

3. A dependency. The way out is two halves in two models: the loss reaches someone with a say (Web, exact), then the rule turns (ClosedCapture, sufficient). They are joined by a reading. The flat map shows one solid arrow.

4. Direction. Counted per relation and direction, the map holds ways out and almost no ways in. Nothing shows how a counted cost stops being counted except through removal, and nothing shows how those with a say come to be drawn from those ahead. For a map meant to show how a joint selection does not come to select for control of its own selection, the inward directions are the ones to draw or to mark blank.

5. Opposites as one line. Three pairs of places (costs / pays, several / one, felt in time / too late) are each one relation's two sides. Drawing them so is the plain form of what Ren asked of 对立统一 on the map, and it removes paired boxes that read as good and bad.
loses_or_risks:
- More unity than the Lean has. One relation gathers predicates from different models (Unread in ClosedCapture, selected-alike in Web). That is a reading unless a join is proved. carried_by with its joined status must be drawn (separate strands where unjoined), or the structure repeats the silent identification it was meant to end.
- A table of ten relations suggests a thousand states and independent switches. Most combinations have no law, and relations depend on one another. Draw only patterns that laws speak of, and blanks as blanks.
- Thresholds are not edges. About a third of the items are exact comparisons of counts (tipping counts, who outnumbers whom, cost against return). They stay as a sentence in "threshold"; the structure does not formalise them.
- Ten relations for 15 places is not a large saving in this region. The claim that relations grow more slowly than places across the atlas (my guess: 20 to 30 against 35 to 40) is an estimate from two shared relations seen, not a count.
- The figure is untested on a person. Ren said yes to the node-link map. The strip of small webs should be made for this one region and put beside it before anything is extended on it.
- Vocabulary. "Relation", "pattern" and "role" are ordinary words; "line", "motif" and "facet" would be new private ones and should not appear.
- My item-to-relation assignments were made in one pass. They need the same settle-and-refute round the 88 decisions had.
scales_to_other_families:
E (Waiting and reciprocity, 10 dynamics): holds as questions, strains as a small web.
- Its selection end is already on region C's r8 by proved identity.
- "Waits on" is a relation between formations, so the grammar fits.
- But its exact laws speak of paths: "gives at step n from every start exactly where no chain of n waits leads into it" (restoring-giving-from-the-worst-start exit 2), plus tolerances and windows. The question form works ("does a chain of withholding lead to it, and how long?"). A glyph with fixed roles can only sketch a chain.

A (Absorption and ending, 29): two parts.
- The World-based dynamics fit well with depends on / gives to / draws on, plus one threshold relation: the level against what the standing draw leaves room to renew. margin-of-a-regime exit 1 is exact; consumption-ends-with-feeders exit 1 is "fed by something itself supported", necessary, with its dropped premise recorded. three-outcomes-of-a-loss is a fork with three outcomes, which a turn holds and an arrow does not. These relations would also place the two region items left unresolved for lack of an origin (persisting-filters-what-was-chosen exit 1, readings-revised-spread-and-locked exit 2).
- At least five entries are about any course and any region, with no roles: attraction-is-not-returning, basins-of-a-determined-law, necessarily-drawn-is-not-returning, every-loss-passes-a-juncture, not-going-out-of-a-region. There the structure breaks as content. They belong in the legend: what "a place you do not leave" and "a fork" mean on every map. A flat list would force them into places.

F (Cycles, 24): 14 have no exit, transition or compose entry, so a place map gets no arrows from them. In relation form most are a third value of an existing relation, not a place. threshold-reading-read-late-alternates is r2 "swings" (never_locked), the condition a checker found no place for. One relation recurs across families: the reading arrives late (reading-a-loss-in-time in B, the stale-rule witness of habit-lock-in-active-inference in C, late-relay-oscillates in F, two-sided-regulation-and-late-reading in H). A flat list splits it between "past turning back" and "cycling".

Not read closely: D, G, most of H.
false_premise:
Three, each partly.

1. "The data structure that projects onto the map." At present nothing projects. The 15 places were written first, with free-text tests, and the 88 items were sorted into them. The map is authored and the data fitted to it. The overlaps and the 12 unresolved items are the residue of that order. The question becomes answerable once the stored thing is the relations and the map is computed.

2. "Pareto frontier", asked of one map. Only the stored structure can be on a frontier, judged by whether it regenerates every projection without loss. The five-minute reader, the one-hour reader and the person holding a real case need different drawings of it. The node-link picture can stay while its data moves under it.

3. "Optimal for human understanding" cannot be settled by design argument, mine included. The last scores of 8 came from AI readers grading AI pages. What can be said from the data is which structure loses less and shows more. Which picture a person understands in five minutes is found by Ren and two or three outside readers looking at both.
